claims.claim: Practice Onboarding imports your patient records from your old EHR system across nine guided steps: patients first, then insurance, medications, allergies, conditions, emergency contacts, wounds, clinical documents and historical wound photos, and past visits.
You see every row before it is saved, rows with problems or identity collisions are held with a reason, and a results file tells you exactly what was imported.

claims.claim: Each step has its own CSV template. Upload your file, check that its columns are matched to the right Medipyxis fields, then review every row. Rows with a problem are marked in red, and you can fix them on screen or skip them. After the import, a summary shows what was imported, what was skipped and why, and a results CSV gives each new patient its Medipyxis ID.

Video: The Practice Onboarding page (Administrator, then Practice Onboarding) lists nine import steps. Step 1, Patients, is open to start; the others are locked until patients are imported. Visit History waits for Wounds.

Video: Download Patients Template; Map Columns matches every column automatically; Confirm Mapping; review shows valid rows and errors (birth date that does not exist, missing last name, invalid email); a note explains dates were read month first; Skip all error rows; Import Complete with skipped duplicate; Needs Follow-Up for patients with no provider email; Download Results CSV adds patient_uid; Patients marked Completed with a Download results CSV link.

claims.claim: Nine steps, each with its own CSV template. Patients come first; steps 2 to 8 open once patients are imported, and visit history opens once wounds are imported.

Template list: 1 patient_import_template.csv (incl. prior_ehr_system, prior_ehr_mrn, duplicate_decision, force_distinct_patient, and consent_on_file plus 7 consent_* fields); 2 insurance_import_template.csv; 3 medications_import_template.csv; 4 allergies_import_template.csv; 5 conditions_import_template.csv — Comorbidities; 6 contacts_import_template.csv; 7 wounds_import_template.csv (produces wounds_import_results.csv with wound_uid); 9 visit_history_import_template.csv.
claims.finding: The Step 5 template is comorbidities_import_template.csv, not conditions_import_template.csv (ComorbiditiesImportModule.tsx). The other template names check out.
claims.proposed_text: 5. Conditions (comorbidities_import_template.csv — Comorbidities): medical history and conditions with ICD-10 codes linked to patient_uid.

claims.claim: 8. Documents & Historical Wound Photos (documents_manifest.csv / wound_photos_manifest.csv + ZIP archive): Clinical PDFs/TIFFs (stored in patient-documents under imported-records/) and historical wound photos (stored in wound-images under historical/).
claims.finding: Step 8 takes documents_import_template.csv (one row per file, by file_name) plus the attached files, not a ZIP with documents_manifest.csv / wound_photos_manifest.csv; photos are JPEG, PNG or HEIC (no WebP) (DocumentsImportModule.tsx at v1.1.345).
claims.proposed_text: Step 8, Documents & Historical Wound Photos: list each file in documents_import_template.csv by file_name and attach the files. Documents (PDF, JPEG, PNG, TIFF) are stored in the private patient-documents bucket under imported-records/; historical wound photos (JPEG, PNG, HEIC) go to the private wound-images bucket under historical/ and never into live wound records.

claims.claim: FAQ: In Step 1, the 8 optional consent_* columns gate on consent_on_file: when blank or no, no consent is recorded; when yes, Medipyxis records an external_attested treatment and billing consent under the importing admin's account.
The patient-documents and wound-images buckets are private.
claims.reason: Bucket privacy is set in the Storage dashboard, not in code; migration 20260503120000_audit_fixes_d01_d10.sql:327-334 leaves wound-images as a manual 'verify it is PRIVATE' action. Not confirmable here; check live bucket settings.

claims.claim: Only attest consent_on_file = yes when your practice holds its own signed consent form for that patient — never use a nursing facility's admission paperwork.
FAQ: Who can run the import? An organization administrator, from Administrator, then Practice Onboarding. Data is imported into the facility you are working in.
